findings.title: upsampled_count is only registered on Discover but is generated for the errors dataset
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to upsampled_count() whenever _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True, and that helper returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset. However the new SnQLFunction is only added to the Discover dataset's function_converter; the errors dataset has its own function converter without upsampled_count. Any events-stats request with dataset=errors on an allowlisted project will therefore fail query validation/building (unknown function) instead of returning upsampled counts.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats receives scoped_dataset (which the dashboard-widget split logic can change to discover or keep as the metrics dataset), but the eligibility check passes the closure variable `dataset` instead of scoped_dataset. When a metrics_performance/metrics_enhanced request is split into a Discover error query, upsampling is wrongly skipped; conversely a transaction-like split can be transformed based on the original dataset even though the executed dataset/query is not error data. The transform decision must be made for the dataset actually executed.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated error filters as error-focused queries
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring search for 'event.type:error', so queries such as '!event.type:error', '-event.type:error', or 'event.type:transaction OR !event.type:error' are classified as error-focused. The endpoint will then rewrite count() to sum(sample_weight) over predominantly transaction/non-error rows, where sample_weight is not meaningful/populated, returning zero or badly undercounted series instead of the real count.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) drops events that have no sample weight
findings.body: The aggregate is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no fallback for rows whose sample_weight is NULL. Allowlisted projects will normally contain historical events and events ingested without client sampling information; ClickHouse sum() ignores NULLs (and yields NULL/0 for an all-NULL bucket), so those events silently disappear from upsampled counts rather than counting as 1 each. A safe aggregate needs a per-row default such as coalesce(sample_weight, 1).

findings.title: Cache key relies on Python hash() and the invalidation helper is never wired up
findings.body: Eligibility is cached under a key built from hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))) and invalidate_upsampling_cache recomputes the same expression, but no code path calls invalidate_upsampling_cache when the project allowlist option changes. Combined with hash-collision risk between different project sets, one project set can briefly serve another set's cached eligibility and, more importantly, allowlist removals keep upsampling (and additions keep not upsampling) until TTL expiry with no invalidation hook despite the helper suggesting otherwise. Use a deterministic, collision-resistant key (e.g. the joined project ids) and either call invalidation on option change or remove the dead helper.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink/subproject file committed
findings.body: This adds a file `sentry-repo` containing only 'Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a', i.e. an accidental nested-repository gitlink. It is unrelated to the upsampling feature, will confuse tooling/checkouts, and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Error-focus detection reads request.GET instead of the actual query being executed
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query inspects request.GET['query'], but _get_event_stats executes the `query` argument passed through get_event_stats_data and the dashboard split logic, which can differ from the raw GET parameter (split code appends 'AND !event.type:transaction', callers can supply modified queries). Eligibility can therefore be decided from a different query than the one sent to Snuba, causing missed upsampling for split error queries or transforms applied to non-error executions. Pass the effective query string into the eligibility check instead of re-reading the request.
